analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: A sustained correction in the AI trade is a major risk to the global economy
key_insights: BofA says investors are increasingly concerned about the sustainability of the AI trade, and the more AI capex rises, the more risks loom. Open questions are whether firms can monetize the investment and whether adoption speed disappoints.
An eventual AI slowdown could hit GDP growth directly and through wealth effects. BofA calls a correction in the AI trade one of the larger risks to the US and global economy.
US GDP growth extends well beyond the net contribution from AI capex, according to BofA's contributions chart.
Tighter global financial conditions are a first-order risk. AI capex and financial conditions are linked, since higher interest rates partly reflect increased supply to finance AI investment.
A tightening of financial conditions from outside the region hurts most where the AI capex boom is not being captured, such as Europe.
BofA argues that with strong US GDP growth spreading beyond AI capex and years of above-potential growth signaling overheating, it is hard to justify the Fed's inaction.
Unclear geopolitical tensions add to the cautious sentiment.
BofA's 3Q26 GDP tracking estimate is 3.4% q/q saar after the advance estimate, against BofA's official forecast of 3.5%. Final sales tracking is 5.0%, vs 3.7% in the official forecast.
In the tracking table, 3Q equipment investment is 20.9% and exports are 5.4%, with imports at 19.7%. Government spending is -5.7% and residential investment is -3.4%.
Today's calendar: September construction spending, October ISM manufacturing, and Fed's Goolsbee moderating a discussion at 11:15.

risk_factors: A sustained correction in the AI trade, through failure to monetize AI investment or slower-than-expected adoption, hitting GDP directly and through wealth effects.
Tighter global financial conditions, tied partly to higher interest rates from the supply needed to finance AI investment.
Uneven impact of tighter financial conditions on regions such as Europe that are not benefiting from the AI capex cycle.
Overheating in the US after years of above-potential growth, with the Fed not acting.
Geopolitical tensions with an unclear path.

geopolitical: BofA cites a lack of clarity around the path of geopolitical tensions as adding to cautious sentiment.
